messages:
ashley: heads up — since ~03:40 UTC we've been seeing SMM watchdog resets on a subset of eu-west GPU racks after last night's BIOS push. nodes keep hard-evicting during boot, provisioning failing. BMCs also are flapping on some hosts. anyone oncall looking?

sam: seeing it on grafana too. evictions spiked at 03:42, p95 boot time jumped from 45s -> 230s.

sam: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/infra/gpu-provisioning?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west (filters: tag=gpu-rack)

maria: FYI noticed BIOS image 2024-11-02-r2 toggled SMM watchdog default from disabled->enabled on some boards. that seems likely.

jordan: confirmed in serial logs for 3 nodes: 
```
[  234.567] SMM watchdog timeout - CPU reset
[  235.103] NVRAM: bios variant r2 applied
[  235.450] BMC heartbeat lost - kvm-session dropped
```

ashley: oof. are those nodes where secureboot also switched state? i saw a couple of attestation failures in the canary group earlier.

maria: secureboot flag was untouched in the image, but the image changed OEM thermal curve which pushes fans slower on idle. combined with SMM watchdog enabling -> short thermal excursions trigger watchdog.

kevin: quick mitigation ideas: 1) pin provisioning to previous BIOS image for new boots; 2) add a temporary exception to autoreviction for boot stage for 10m; 3) rollback canaries.

ashley: agreed. we should stop the rollout and start a controlled rollback for the eu-west GPU pools. i'll pause the fleet rollout now.

oncall-bot: @eng-infra-ops acknowledged incident #INC-2024-497 and paged oncall. runbook 'bios-rollback' recommended.

eng-infra-ops: executed fleetctl rollouts pause --selector region=eu-west --campaign bios-2024-11-02. canaries paused.

jordan: i'm prepping a small rollback job to r1-bios-2024-10-28 for affected racks. runbook snippet: 
```
fleetctl set-bios-image --image r1-bios-2024-10-28 --filter "region=eu-west AND tag=gpu-rack" --concurrency 5
fleetctl watch --filter "job=rollback and region=eu-west"
```

sam: reminder: if we disable evictions we risk leaving unhealthy nodes in the pool -> job failures. maybe set autoreplace=false but leave healthcheck alerts on.

maria: agreed. propose: autoreplace=false for 15m during rollback window, evictions still allowed after node passes boot healthchecks.

kevin: what's customer impact now?

ashley: estimate: ~8% GPU capacity in eu-west unavailable, provisioning errors causing ~12% job retries. affecting a handful of enterprise tenants with reserved capacity; alerting customers on status page.

maria: cost note: if we burst to other regions to cover load, expect ~$6-9k/day additional infra spend until rollback completes.

jordan: rollback started for rack ids: eu-gpu-rack-07, eu-gpu-rack-11, eu-gpu-rack-15. first batch (5 nodes) done; boots look healthy so far.

ashley: good. ops checklist: 1) keep canaries in isolation; 2) monitor SMM reset logs; 3) revert OEM thermal curve in next image; 4) add preflight test for SMM watchdog bit on future images.

sam: adding preflight to CI: ipmi check + serial log grep for SMM bit and fan curve values. will open PR.

eng-infra-ops: canary health at +13m: 0 new SMM resets, provision success 98%. holding rollback cadence.

kevin: ping @product regarding communication. we should post an incident update: brief impact + ETA for full rollback.

ashley: posted update to status.redwood.ai and sent a customer email to affected reserved accounts.

maria: follow-ups: create an infra alert to catch OEM thermal curve diffs on future BIOS images; and add a clause in firmware onboarding checklist about watchdog default state.

jordan: logs for forensics: 
```
journalctl -u bmc | grep -i "reboot\|watchdog" --since "03:30"
ipmitool -H <bmc> -U admin sel elist
serial-console dump: /var/log/serial/eu-gpu-rack-11-2024-11-03.log
```

sam: thumbs up. i'll rebalance a couple of lower-priority jobs to us-central to reduce customer impact while rollback finishes.

ashley: thanks team. will keep thread updated. next update in ~20m or on any regression. :thumbsup:
